title: Special council authorizes closed session on potential litigation
subtitle: Short meeting with no delegations, no declared conflicts of interest and routine by-law confirmation before adjournment.
overview: Kitchener City Council held a brief special meeting that began at 4:00 p.m. and adjourned at 4:09 p.m. The Mayor chaired, gave the land acknowledgement, and noted that notice had been given to all members of Council. No one declared a pecuniary interest, there were no delegations, and the Mayor had no business or updates to report.

The only substantive decision was to hold a closed meeting immediately after the special meeting to consider a potential litigation matter, as permitted under Section 239 (2) (e) of the Municipal Act, 2001. Council approved this {{vote:m1}}. The public minutes do not describe the matter, and no outcome was reported from the closed session.

Council also passed the by-law confirming its actions and proceedings for July 28, 2026 (By-law 2026-093), which is routine. For residents, the meeting shows that Council is considering a legal matter in private. Any decision arising from it would need to be reported publicly at a later meeting.

decisions.detail: Council agreed to hold a closed meeting right after the special meeting to consider a potential litigation matter under Section 239 (2) (e) of the Municipal Act, 2001 {{vote:m1}}.

debate: No delegations were registered, so no residents or groups spoke to Council at this meeting.
When the Mayor asked for discussion on the motion to go in camera for a potential litigation matter, the transcript records no comments before the vote.
No councillor declared a pecuniary interest, and the remaining motions on by-laws and adjournment also went to a vote without recorded discussion.
